newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Samsung sets $300 mln convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: Samsung sets $300 mln convertible bond.

text.p: Samsung Electronics Co has placed a US$300 million convertible bond issue convertible into GDRs or new shares of Samsung Electronics, lead manager and sole bookrunner Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
Samsung Securities was joint lead manager.
The bond was structured as a zero coupon puttable instrument with an issue price of par and redeemable at par.
The bond is puttable on the fifth anniversary at 131.057 to yield 5.56 percent annually, or 80 basis points below the corresponding U.S. Treasury bond.

The conversion price is 123,635 won, based on a fixed rate of exchange of 888.5 won to US$1.00, or US$69.575 per GDR, which is equivalent to a conversion ratio of approximately 35.93 shares per US$5,000 bond and represents an initial conversion premium of 15 percent over the Samsung Electronics GDR price at the time of pricing, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
The bond is callable after two years subject to a 135 percent hurdle.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said the bond was the largest ever for a Korean corporate and the largest zero coupon issue for an Asian issuer.
